chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I heard him saying: There is nothing except that there is about it a Book or a Sunna.
There is nothing [of legal ruling] except that there is about it a Book or a Sunna.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: Sunnah, referring to the traditions and practices of the Prophet and Imams as a source of law
key_terms.كِتَابٌ: The Book (Quran), referring to divine scripture as a source of law

ai.seo_question: What is the basis for all legal rulings in Shia Islam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishes the principle of *kaffat al-shay'* (comprehensiveness), asserting that no issue remains without a specific ruling in the Quran or the Sunnah. In Shia Usul al-Fiqh, this serves as the basis for the belief that the divine sources are sufficient for all legal and practical matters, whether explicitly stated or derivable through ijtihad. It underscores the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in interpreting these sources to address every aspect of human life.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/-] al-Kafi: Ali from Muhammad b. Isa from Yunus from Hammad from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, he (Hammad) said:
I heard him saying: there is nothing except there is about it [a ruling in the] Book or Sunna.
